subject: Re: Packaging options — feature gates and tier switch mechanics
content:

From: Emma Rossi <emma.rossi@medicore.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Subject: Packaging guidance — need help choosing a tier

Hi Marcus,

Quick follow-up from our product review yesterday — we liked Redwood's Dedicated offering but are unsure which package to pick. Our immediate needs are: low-latency inference for triage flows (peak 50 qps), audit logs for compliance, and the ability to gate premium features behind flags for select customers.

Two questions:
- Can we start on Compact (saves cost) and later turn on a subset of features without a full upgrade?
- Do you support per-route feature flags so we can gate heavier models only for specific endpoints?

Also cc'ing John (ops) who will own deployment.

Thanks,
Emma
Product Lead — Medicore Health

Message 2 — 2026-11-08T13:30:00Z
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Rossi <emma.rossi@medicore.ai>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@medicore.ai>
Subject: Re: Packaging guidance — need help choosing a tier

Hi Emma — great to hear from you and glad yesterday's session was useful. Short answers up front, then a recommended path: 

1) Can you start on Compact and enable features later? Yes — Compact supports per-route entitlements and we can gate features via our routing policies and per-route quotas. There are two practical levers: 
   - Entitlement flags (soft gating) — flips within the same package, no downtime.
   - Model/instance upgrades (hard upgrade) — moving from Compact -> Full adds extra GPU capacity and higher concurrency.

2) Per-route feature flags? Yes. You can route specific endpoints to higher-capacity model variants (or to Dedicated pools) via route rules in the Console.

Recommendation: Start Compact + enable the audit logs add-on now. Keep two conservatively sized Dedicated slots reserved (burst capacity) and use feature flags to route only the triage endpoint to those slots. That keeps base spend low while giving you predictable headroom for low-latency bursts.

I've attached a short options PDF with estimated monthly cost ranges and toggles. If you want, I can loop in Karthik (works on capacity planning) and Priya (enterprise packaging) to scope a formal proposal and a short Mutual Action Plan.

Attachment: medicore-package-options-v2.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Marcus
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Message 4 (internal) — 2026-11-09T09:05:00Z
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Subject: Medicore — upgrade heuristics, latency SLOs and prorate ask (internal)

Karthik / Priya — looping you both in. Medicore (attached thread) is considering Compact + per-route gating for a triage endpoint. They need:

- p95 < 150ms at peaks ~50 qps when routed to burst slots
- Clear billing/proration language if they switch from Compact -> Full mid-term

My read: we can hit p95 < 150ms if we reserve two Dedicated burst instances and route triage traffic there — that'll meet SLO for 50 qps with modest queuing. Karthik, can you validate the capacity numbers (GPU class assumption: A10s equivalent) + whether two burst instances is the right ask? Also advise about autoscale policy we should recommend.

Priya, procurement wants to know if we offer a simple credit model: apply the remaining Compact commitment pro-rated toward the Full commitment for the remainder of the billing period, no double-billing. We typically do a net-credit (remaining dollars moved to new commitment) for enterprise upgrades — is that OK here or do we need a formal amendment? They may push for mid-term refund instead.

Why this matters: Medicore is price-sensitive but strategic — small initial commit, high potential expansion. Happy to offer a short-term pilot with a modest discount if it helps conversion, but want to align on guardrails first.

Thanks — Marcus

Message 5 — 2026-11-09T16:40:00Z
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Rossi <emma.rossi@medicore.ai>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@medicore.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Packaging guidance — need help choosing a tier (summary & MAP)

Hi Emma / John — thanks for the clarifying questions and for the patience while I pulled internal ops + packaging together. Summary and next steps below.

What we propose (short pilot path):
- Start on Compact + Audit Logs add-on.
- Configure two Dedicated burst slots (A10-equivalent) reserved for the triage endpoint; route via per-route feature flag.
- Target SLO: p95 < 150ms for triage when routed to burst slots. Karthik validated capacity assumptions and suggested an autoscale policy that adds a single burst node at 20 qps and a second at 40 qps to keep p95 in range.
- Billing/proration: we will apply remaining Compact dollars pro-rated as a credit toward a Full commitment for the same billing period (no double-billing). A one-page amendment will document the credit.
- Pilot discount: 10% off Compact list prices for the first 3 months, convertible into a standard commit if you upgrade.

Attachments: feature-flag-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains the route rules and suggested flags for rollout; medicore-package-options-v2.pdf — updated with cost numbers and the amendment language.

Next steps / asks for Medicore:
1) Confirm you want to start the pilot and accept the 10% introductory discount.
2) Share preferred start date (we need ~10 business days to provision burst slots and set up audit log retention).
3) Confirm John will be the ops contact for Console access and entitlement testing.

If you confirm, Priya will send the one-page amendment and I will set up a short technical kickoff with Karthik and our infra on call.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
